lines.english: The great mausoleum in Talas,
Beside the great mausoleum,
For Manas, who had gone to the other world,
She offered a prayer, saying, ‘Amen,’
The sura called ‘Tabbat,’
She recited swiftly, as though astonished.
When she looked this way:
Argyns and Kyrgyz were deep in thought,
It was the time when they were encamped,
Kumis by day, girls by night,
It was a time of such things.
Wearing marten caps in matching pairs,
It was a time when they swayed about,
The Kyrgyz, joining in lament,
It was a time when they lived in delight.
At that time the Kyrgyz people
Had whole sable skins
Slit open and taken off,
A garden they had planted in Talas,
It was flourishing luxuriantly.
At that time among the Kyrgyz,
Even a poor man drove a thousand sheep,
An old woman chewed fat tail,
Of the Kyrgyz, seething with abundance,
Which of their troubles could I tell?
With kelengker headgear and broad hips,
lines.note: Uncertain: kelengker appears to name a style of women's headdress.

lines.english: The Kyrgyz daughters-in-law were beautiful,
In red dresses, with waists like the moon,
The Kyrgyz daughters were beautiful,
In black coats and white felt hats,
The Kyrgyz people were beautiful,
There was much rice from black grain,
There was much silver from their tin,
There were more foxes than white hares,
They had much wealth piled by the threshold,
They wore fox and ermine.
The orphan had grown to maturity,
And had joined his head to the people,
Semetey had become the leader of the people.
Aichurok did not know this,
She stood amazed at this sight,
What their heroes wore
Were black caps of blue lynx fur,
All their heroes
Were alike, dark blue throughout.
They had swift steeds beneath them,
When six or seven came together,
They had the strength of Chynkozhol.
lines.note: Uncertain: Chynkozhol is likely a proper name or a fixed epic epithet.

lines.english: What they all rode
Were black bay battle-horses,
With sieve-like lungs and bronze arms.
lines.note: The line uses compressed heroic imagery; the precise force of ‘sieve-like lungs’ is uncertain.

lines.english: Willow-rich Ken-Kol and Talas,
Seeing those lands, she rejoiced,
And now Aichurok was content.
